class_name: 否定-無意味-ドコロデハナイ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Sweeps an activity off the table as untimely: circumstances are so pressing that the named thing is unthinkable — 旅行どころじゃない, 走るどころではなかった. It usually carries an irritation that the neutral 〜ている場合ではない lacks, and the の話じゃない variants add scorn. 〜どころか is a different pattern, correcting a mistaken expectation rather than dismissing an activity.

examples.ruby: 締[し]め切[き]り前[まえ]で、旅行[りょこう]どころじゃないんだ。
examples.english: I'm up against a deadline — a trip is completely out of the question.

examples.ruby: 腰[こし]を痛[いた]めて、しばらく走[はし]るどころではなかった。
examples.english: I hurt my back, and for a while running was the last thing I could do.

examples.ruby: 風呂[ふろ]の水[みず]があふれて、夕飯[ゆうはん]の支度[したく]どころじゃない。
examples.english: The bath's overflowing — getting dinner ready is out of the question.

patterns.usage_note: Disqualifies something as not deserving the name: what is on offer falls hopelessly short — 食えたもんじゃない, 読めたものじゃない. In this sense it typically follows a potential form, with the contracted たもんじゃない as the spoken shape. Where the sibling どころじゃない says an activity is untimely, this says the thing itself is unfit; after 分かる the same shape gives a separate idiom, 〜か分かったもんじゃない, "there's no telling".

examples.ruby: あの店[みせ]の魚[さかな]は生臭[なまぐさ]くて、食[く]えたもんじゃない。
examples.english: The fish at that place reeks — it's not fit to eat.

examples.ruby: この字[じ]は崩[くず]しすぎていて、とても読[よ]めたものじゃない。
examples.english: This handwriting is so scrawled you haven't a hope of reading it.

examples.ruby: 隣[となり]の工事[こうじ]がうるさくて、夜[よる]も眠[ねむ]れたもんじゃない。
examples.english: The building work next door is so loud I can't get any sleep at night.
